original_interpretation: Frames API returns one fact per entity per calendar period, enabling cross-company tables (e.g. revenue of every filer for CY2025), with approximate calendar alignment.
evidence_found: "The xbrl/frames API aggregates one fact for each reporting entity that is last filed that most closely fits the calendrical period requested." ... URL pattern ".../frames/us-gaap/AccountsPayableCurrent/USD/CY2019Q1I.json" ... "Data users should be mindful different reporting start and end dates for facts contained in a frame." (EDGAR APIs page)
correction: A frame is per taxonomy + concept + unit (e.g. us-gaap/Revenues/USD), and only non-custom taxonomy facts are aggregated. So one frame does not give 'revenue of every filer': filers using different revenue tags, IFRS (ifrs-full) or non-USD units (e.g. TSMC in TWD) fall into other frames.

original_interpretation: SEC limits undeclared automated tools; researcher's scripted paging of SIC 3674 list was blocked, so the full count was not obtained.
evidence_found: "Automated access must comply with SEC.gov's Privacy and Security Policy, as described in the Developer FAQs." (EDGAR APIs page). Checker's own browser request to browse-edgar?SIC=3674 returned: "Your Request Originates from an Undeclared Automated Tool ... SEC reserves the right to limit requests originating from undeclared automated tools."
correction: SEC's rate-limiting of undeclared automated tools is confirmed (reproduced by the checker). The claim that the count could not be obtained is a statement about this research run, not about SEC data: the documented bulk submissions.zip would allow the count.
notes: Classification: the second half is a process note about our own research run, not an industry fact; better recorded as notes or an 'unknown' claim. The same API page lists a bulk submissions.zip ('public EDGAR filing history for all filers'), which includes SIC codes, so a full SIC-3674 count is obtainable through the documented bulk route.

original_interpretation: Reg S-K Item 101 requires segment-focused business description incl. dependence on key products/customers, only to the extent material; no requirement to name customers.
evidence_found: "focusing upon the registrant's dominant segment or each reportable segment ... only information material to an understanding of the business taken as a whole is required. Disclosure may include ... (i) Revenue-generating activities, products and/or services, and any dependence on ... key products, services, product families or customers, including governmental customers" (17 CFR 229.101(c)(1), eCFR current)
notes: No customer-naming requirement appears in current 229.101(c). Corroboration (law-firm alert, not added as a source): Wilson Sonsini says the 2020 amendments (Release 33-10825, effective 2020-11-09) deleted 'the requirement to list the name of any customer with sales equal to 10 percent or more of the registrant's consolidated revenues' (https://www.wsgr.com/en/insights/amendments-to-regulation-s-k-disclosure-requirements.html). The quoted '(vi) Dependence on one or a few major customers' is in 101(h)(4), which covers smaller reporting companies only. Item 101 applies to domestic registrants; FPIs use Form 20-F Item 4 (FR 85 FR 63727 fn 12). eCFR HTML was blocked; text read via eCFR renderer API.

original_interpretation: TWSE/TPEx-listed companies must input monthly operating revenue into MOPS before the 10th of the following month, under SEA Art. 36.
evidence_found: "1 Monthly sales revenues ... 2 Other listing companies on the TSEC and GTSM ... 2 Operating revenue（Issuers shall announce consolidated operating revenue after adopting IFRSs） ... Must input relevant information into the Market Observation Post System (MOPS) prior to the 10th day of the following month ... 1Paragraph 1 and 4, Article 36 of the Securities and Exchange Act" (FSC list, p.1)
notes: Current statute matches: SEA Art. 36 para 1(3): "Within the first ten days of each calendar month, publicly announce and file with the Competent Authority the operating status for the preceding month." (MOJ English law database). The FSC list is dated 2013-07-16; TSEC/GTSM are the old names of TWSE/TPEx.

original_interpretation: Listed companies file CPA-reviewed Q1-Q3 consolidated reports to MOPS within 45 days of quarter-end.
evidence_found: "Q1 financial report Q2 financial report Q3 financial report ... 1 Quarterly Consolidated financial report reviewed by CPAs ... Must transmit it to the MOPS in electronic file format and file it to the FSC in paper file format within 45 days after the end of the first, second, and third quarters of each fiscal year" (FSC list, item 5)
notes: Current SEA Art. 36 para 1(2) confirms: "Within 45 days after the end of the first, second, and third quarters of each fiscal year, publicly announce and register ... financial reports ... reviewed by a CPA and reported to the board of directors." FSC list adds that Emerging-board and unlisted public companies are exempt from Q1/Q3 reports.

original_interpretation: TWSE/TPEx-listed companies transmit audited annual financial report to MOPS within three months of FY-end.
evidence_found: "7 Yearly financial report 1 Yearly parent company only and consolidated financial report audited by CPAs ... 1 Companies whose stocks are listed on the TSEC or GTSM must transmit it to the MOPS in electronic file format and file it to the FSC in paper file format within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year" (FSC list)

original_interpretation: TWSE assigns category at 50% of operating income over last two FYs (or 80% latest year) and reviews categories every two years.
evidence_found: English Point 5: "The TWSE will conduct a periodic review of the industry category of all listed companies on a biyearly basis." Chinese Point 5 (prevails): "本公司每年定期調整各上市公司之產業類別" (adjusts every year). English note: "In case of any discrepancy between the Chinese version ... and this English translation, the Chinese version shall prevail."
correction: Review frequency is annual (每年), not every two years. The 50% (both of the last two fiscal years) / 80% (latest fiscal year) assignment rules are correct.
notes: The 50%/80% rules are confirmed (Point 3; Chinese: '超過百分之五十以上' in each of the two most recent fiscal years). Superseding claim added with a contradictions record.
